Vertex — Conversion Decline Investigation

iOS · Jan–Jul 2026
Summary 1. User mix 2. US decline 3. Build 1.28.1 4. Economy 4b. Cash spike 5. IAP Explorers
Executive Summary

First-time purchase conversion down ~40–60% since Feb — driven by a build, not traffic quality.

Two forces compound: user mix shifting away from the US, and a real conversion drop within the US starting the week build 1.28.1 shipped.

Lead hypothesis: 1.28.1's FTUE changes (Fridge discounted 80%, progression condition loosened to accept any cheaper product) raised the barrier to a player's first purchase, while repeat purchasing held steady — a first-purchase acquisition problem, not general fatigue. A later economy change (post 1.30.3) compounded it by increasing cash held.

01

User mix shift

US install share fell 21.0% → ~12% (Jan→Jun) — our best-converting market, shrinking fast.

US install share vs conversion

Why it matters

US converts at 5–9%; replacement markets (Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Russia) sit under 2.5%. Mix shift alone drags the blend down — driven by specific scaling campaigns — but it's only part of the story (§2).

03

Build 1.28.1 — the inflection point

A same-month, controlled comparison of app versions — and the full build-over-time trend.

Same-month conversion by version — March, May, June

Each colour = one calendar month, so within a colour, seasonality/geo/campaign mix are held constant. March shows the 1.27.1→1.28.1→1.28.2 step. May and June confirm conversion never recovers to pre-1.28.1 levels even as later builds (1.30.3, 1.31.1, 1.34.0) scale to full volume — it settles lower and keeps drifting down.

What shipped in 1.28.1 (live 14 Mar 2026)

FTUE — Phase 1
Loosened early cash milestones: cashEarned_250 → 100, removed cashEarned_600 step. These were plausible first-purchase triggers.
FTUE Step 23
Changed Product-screen auto-open logic and progression gating.
FTUE Step 27
Fridge discounted 80% — removes the need to buy cash to afford it, directly undercutting a cash-purchase trigger point.
FTUE Step 24
Condition changed from orderedFruityBites to orderedProducts_3 — players can now progress by ordering any (often cheaper) product instead of the one that used to nudge a purchase.
A/B framework
Intrusive-ads & delivery-timing tests migrated Metica → Firebase.
Technical
Reworked IAP verification system — worth ruling out as a measurement artifact.

Conversion across every major build, with cohort size marked

Bars = install volume that month (right axis); line = conversion % (left axis). Conversion never recovers to the Feb (1.26.4) baseline even as later builds (1.30.3, 1.31.1, 1.34.0) scale to full volume.

Why we believe this is the primary cause

Decline is first-purchase-specific (repeat held steady, §5), version-specific (same-month step), and timed to the release. A pricing/seasonality story wouldn't produce all three at once.

04

The economy loosened after 1.30.3

A second, compounding driver: players holding more cash, reducing the need to buy.

After 1.30.3, median cash held increased — weakening the incentive for that first currency purchase, especially for cash/energy bundles. Compounding, not origin — decline predates 1.30.3 by ~2 months.

04b

Digging into why cash balance spiked

Two independent cuts of the data — an A/B test and a plain weekend/weekday split — both point to the same thing: players are simply earning more cash, faster, in specific contexts. That's consistent with (and likely a contributor to) the economy loosening described above.

A. VIP Rush Event: "Non-VIP" bucket holds meaningfully less cash than the 3 active-day variants

Comparing the 4 vipRushEvent variants against each other (users with no exposure to the test excluded), median cash balance for the Non-VIP bucket is lowest at 26 of 28 shop levels — and the gap widens as players progress, from roughly even at level 2–6 to a 15–20% gap by level 29. The same pattern holds for cash earned and spent (27/28 levels each), meaning Non-VIP players are less economically active in both directions, not just holding less.

Point A — read: at any given shop level, being in an active variant (Tue/Thu/Sat) of the VIP Rush Event correlates with meaningfully higher cash earned, spent, and held than the Non-VIP/inactive bucket.

B. Independent of any A/B test: weekends show a sharp jump in cash earned/spent/balance from level 6 onward

Looking at the whole population (no test grouping at all), weekend cash earned is ~44% higher than weekday on average, spent ~35% higher, and balance ~26% higher. Critically, this effect is near-zero at shop levels 2–5 (the FTUE window) and switches on sharply at level 6, then holds steady for the rest of the game — consistent with longer weekend play sessions driving more economy throughput once players are past onboarding.

Cash earned — weekday vs weekend

Cash balance — weekday vs weekend

Because Saturday is one of the VIP Rush Event's active-day variants, part of finding A may simply be riding this natural weekend effect rather than the event itself — worth isolating Tuesday/Thursday (weekday actives) from Saturday (weekend active) before crediting the event alone.

What this means for the cash-balance spike

Neither of these fully explains the build-level economy loosening from §4 on its own — both are relative comparisons (variant vs variant, weekend vs weekday) within the same time period, not a before/after view across builds. But they show the in-game economy is highly sensitive to session context (which day, which test bucket), which makes it very plausible that a small tuning change around 1.31.1 (drop rates, event frequency, reward sizing) could produce a system-wide increase in cash held. Recommended next step: re-run the median-cash-by-build query (already written earlier) split by weekday vs weekend to confirm the 1.30.3 jump holds after controlling for this day-of-week effect.

05

First-purchase decline on our biggest IAPs

The top 3 products drive ~72% of all first purchases. Their conversion is falling — and the two most front-loaded ones break exactly at 1.28.1.

First-time purchase conversion % — pick your own IAPs (monthly cohorts)

Weekly break — first purchase vs repeat, pick your own IAP

Remove Ads All's first-purchase conversion breaks the week of 14 Mar; repeat conversion keeps rising through the same window. The change hurt acquisition of new payers, not willingness of existing ones.

First purchases are front-loaded to day 0

ProductDay 0By D1
Starter Pack is a day-0-or-never product (77% on day 0). Any disruption to the day-0 FTUE moment shows up almost instantly and completely — which is exactly the signature we see.

Blended conversion — first-time vs repeat, monthly

Blended conversion peaked in February (3.46%) and has declined every month since to 2.34% by June — a steady, real conversion decline rather than a one-off dip. This is the rate driving the absolute drop in new payers, since installs alone didn't fall nearly as much.

E · Product conversion & market share (weekly / monthly cohorts)

Finding: Remove Ads All + Starter Pack drive ~54% of first purchases and both break the same week.
Finding: Remove Ads All and Starter Pack drive ~54% of all first purchases and both break at the same week — the two most fragile pillars of the funnel. Switch to "US only" — the same March break shows up, unchanged, confirming it isn't a blended-country artifact.

F · Where each IAP's revenue comes from (by shop level)

Finding: Starter Pack/Remove Ads All's early-level revenue share collapsed right at March.
Finding: Starter Pack and Remove Ads All concentrate revenue in early levels (Starter Pack: ~11% of its own revenue from level 3 alone; Remove Ads All peaks around levels 3-5) — both are effectively early-game products. The Manager Pass and Winter Pass lines are nearly flat across levels 12-28 with no single peak — they're bought steadily by longer-tenured players throughout the mid-late game, not tied to any one level.

Month-over-month, this early-game share collapsed right at March: Starter Pack's revenue from levels 1-3 fell from 31.5% (Jan) → 25.6% (Feb) → just 6.5% (Mar) → under 1% by April/May. Remove Ads All shows the same break: 21.8% → 24.6% → 4.3% → under 1%. The early-game monetization moment for both products essentially disappeared the same month build 1.28.1 shipped — direct product-level evidence for the FTUE-change hypothesis, not just a conversion-rate coincidence.
